query: What features can be extracted to train a model to predict a review's score?

per_column.name: overall_sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: Sentiment is a strong, well-grounded predictor of a numeric review score; values match the source texts.

per_column.name: review_tone_extremity
per_column.rationale: Adds a graded intensity axis beyond binary polarity, useful for regressing on score. Slight redundancy with polarity but distinct granularity; readings are sound.

per_column.name: repurchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repurchase intent correlates with satisfaction. But 'False' is asserted for rows where the text is simply silent (e.g. dog food, taffy) rather than 'unknown', conflating absence-of-signal with negative intent, weakening groundedness.

per_column.name: taste_flavor_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Taste satisfaction is a meaningful score driver with a not_applicable escape; sample values are well supported.

per_column.name: flavor_strength_perception
per_column.rationale: Useful niche axis. However labeling silent rows 'balanced' (e.g. dog food, taffy) over-asserts a specific perception the text does not state; better handled as not_applicable/unknown.

per_column.name: bitterness_presence
per_column.rationale: Highly imbalanced (97.6% false), near-constant, so weak analytical leverage for this query. Values are defensibly grounded/negative-by-default.

per_column.name: texture_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Reasonable secondary quality axis with proper not_applicable handling; sample values well grounded.

per_column.name: product_quality_judgment
per_column.rationale: Quality judgment strongly tracks star rating and is a good predictor; readings are sound though somewhat correlated with expectation_match.

per_column.name: product_efficacy
per_column.rationale: Useful for supplements/pet products. But applying 'mild_positive_effect' to a plain dog-food quality review stretches an efficacy frame the text does not invoke.

per_column.name: ease_of_use
per_column.rationale: Mostly not_applicable (79%), limited leverage for food-review score prediction, but grounded with proper NA handling.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Category enables grouping and controls for product-type effects on score; extractions from text are sound.

per_column.name: usage_context
per_column.rationale: Context (gift, pet, baby) is a genuine grouping axis; values reasonably inferred, though 'personal_use' is a heavy default that may over-assert on silent rows.

per_column.name: expectation_match
per_column.rationale: Meaningful driver of score but substantially redundant with product_quality_judgment; values are well grounded.

per_column.name: novelty_value
per_column.rationale: Plausible minor feature. 'True' for the confection/root-beer rows is a soft inference; borderline but acceptable, though somewhat speculative.

per_column.name: reviewer_expertise_signal
per_column.rationale: Expertise proxy is a plausible feature. Labeling the detailed confection review 'expert_enthusiast' is a defensible inference from richness of text.

per_column.name: review_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Detail level is a reasonable style feature (borders on a length proxy, limiting novelty for score prediction) but is well grounded in the observable text.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide multiple genuine axes (sentiment, tone extremity, quality judgment, taste satisfaction, category, usage context) that would meaningfully help model a review's score, satisfying analytical usefulness overall despite some redundancy (polarity/extremity, quality/expectation_match) and a few weak near-constant columns (bitterness_presence, ease_of_use). Groundedness is generally strong and sample values track the source texts, with appropriate not_applicable/unknown handling in several columns. The main weakness is a tendency to assert confident defaults (repurchase_intent=false, flavor_strength=balanced, product_efficacy applied to non-efficacy products) on rows where the text is silent, which introduces mild hallucination rather than using an unknown value.
